subject: Day 28: week 5; peak-crying curve approaches
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 28. Four weeks old; week five opens. You are near the front edge of the peak-crying curve — inconsolable evenings peak around six weeks. This is normal and self-limited; it is not a parenting failure.

Action items
- Confirm the 1-month visit happened and the growth chart is on track. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Read about the 5 S's (swaddle, side hold, shush, swing, suck) so you have a settling sequence ready for hard nights. AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- Pre-schedule the 2-month well visit for day 56-70 if not yet done; vaccines will include HepB, RV, DTaP, Hib, PCV, and IPV. AAP on immunizations: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Run active daycare or nanny interviews if returning to work in 7-11 weeks. Care.com: https://www.care.com/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Inconsolable evening crying with no clear cause — peak crying is normal and clusters at this age. Hiccups during feeds; wet sneezing.
- [low concern] More sustained head lifts in tummy time; brief tracking across the visual field; social smiles.
- [monitor] Forceful arching during or after feeds, painful spit-up, or feeding refusal despite hunger cues — possible GERD or cow's-milk-protein intolerance; raise at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Bloody-mucus stool (possible CMPI or anal fissure), or sustained refusal of feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Enroll in or waitlist a Music Together class near you; live group music from around six weeks is the highest-evidence music intervention for prelinguistic gains. Music Together: https://www.musictogether.com/
- Hold a high-contrast card 8-12 inches away and move it slowly through 180 degrees to draw out visual tracking. AAP HealthyChildren on movement, birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Face-to-face talking with slow, exaggerated expressions — the most reliable way to elicit an early social smile. AAP HealthyChildren on infant senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day cumulative across short bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: peak crying at about six weeks.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit (OB clearance for exercise; EPDS rescreen).
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
